OUR scIeNTIFIc PRINCIPLE
We engineered E.coli with a novel light-harvesting system (NPM) inspired by
photosynthetic bacteria. By embedding NuoK (electron transporter), PufL
(reaction center), and MgP (chlorophyll analog), we created a light-dependent
electron chain. This system uses methanol as an electron donor to produce
formaldehyde and NADH-key precursors for hydrogen synthesis.
METABOLIC ENGINEERING MASTERY
• GSH Overproduction: Knocking out gpmA halts competing pathways, while
gshA/gshB overexpression floods cells with glutathione. This traps formaldehyde
as S-hydroxymethylglutathione, driving its conversion to formate.
• FHL Hyperactivation: Derepressing fhIA (activator) and removing iscR/hycA (inhibitors)
unleashes the FHL complex. This enzyme system splits formate into H2 and COz with
industrial-scale efficiency.

Club Grenade is a fast-paced multiplayer action game which a group of friends
and family of all ages, at a maximum of four players, can enjoy. In the game, each
player controls a character who infiltrates a high-tech facility and fights
through waves of enemies with grenades only. The game has a cartoony art-style

characters, four types of enemies, five types of
grenades and a single large level with three stages,
all fully animated and textured. The players win if
they defeat all enemies and exit the level, or lose if
all players have been defeated.

Background
Stem cell therapy is a promising approach for healing many diseases.
In order to improve the efficiency of cell therapy, cell migration process
is of interest to understand. Since cell migration requires the generation
of traction force, this project focuses on the improvement and
application of traction force assay.

Overview
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques allow intra-operative monitoring of the ablation procedure during cardiovascular electrophysiology (EP). However, currently it is still
challenging to carry out effective catheterization under MRI environment. We present an MR-safe robot for intra-cardiac EP intervention. The robot actuation features small
hysteresis, effective force transmission and quick response. Experimental evaluation has verified its capability to precisely tele-manipulate a standard clinically used EP catheter.

RoboFish
Presented by BREED HKU - bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong
Aim
This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore
the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
Our current objective through this endeavor is to
learn about the biomechanics of fish and other
underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand
how the movements are affected by different
variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The
model can be applied in surveillance systems and the
study of marine biology.
Hardware
RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered
by a battery.
The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that
moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion
of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was
designed by the mechanical team to translate the
rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion.
In the future, more features such as remote controlling
and surveillance systems aim to be added.
Figure 1. Initial Design.
Software
Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.
Background research on simulators.
Next stage:
Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment
of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the
model).
Through simulation, variation of different parameters of
the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed
and energy efficiency.
Design
The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess
the following characteristics:
Streamlined body.
Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between
separate components.
Low weight.
Floating stability and buoyancy.

Conclusion and Applications
We believe that there are several applications of our project for research in the academic world. Our model can be
used to analyze marine biology through exploration of the sea. A significant possibility is thus the application of
surveillance systems, not just in ecosystems research, but also in the navy.

ABSTRACT
Scoliosis is a medical
condition where a
person's spine has a
sideways curve. It
usually occurs before
puberty and prevents the
lungs from functioning
properly in severe cases.
Scoliosis is typically
diagnosed from X-ray
images, but diagnostic
X-rays increase the risk
of developmental
problems and cancer in
those exposed. This
project aims to obviate
children's X-ray
exposure in the early
diagnosis of scoliosis by
generating X-ray images
of children's backs from
the corresponding
harmless RGB-D images
rather than capturing the
X-ray images directly
from the children. An
RGB-D image of a back
combines a standard
RGB image with its
depth image, and the
depth image consists of
the distance between
each point on the back
and the camera to track
the spine. In this project,
a deep learning model
based on HRNet was
built and trained to
detect landmark
locations of the backs on
the RGB-D images first.
With the detected
landmarks, the X-ray
images of the children's
backs were eventually
synthesized from the
corresponding RGB-D
images by another deep
learning model that was
built and trained based
on the pix2pix model.

More on IMU
IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures
and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and
sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically
used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading
reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles
(UAVs), among many others, and spacecraft, including
satellites and landers. !!!
An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear
acceleration using one or more accelerometers and
rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also
include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a
heading reference. Typical configurations contain one
accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each
of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat
uses a library called RTIMULib to implement the interface
for reading from its IMU.

Func 3: HomeKit Integration
By installing a tiny server called HomeBridge on Raspberry Pi, we
can accept requests from Apple's Home App and send data back
to Home App. We can run python scripts to poll from SenseHat's
sensors regularly and output the result to HomeBridge.
Function Implementations
Func 1: Digital Level Meter
This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As
there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch
and roll values from the board. When the program detects that
roll is bigger than 45 or smaller than -45 degrees, the program
will switch to pitch measure mode. In this mode, a line will be
displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally.
When roll is between -45° and 45°, the program will switch to
pitch and roll measure mode. There will be two circles
displayed on SenseHat, and they will become closer if pitch
and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles
will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning
that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.

OUR PROJECT AIM
This project aims to design and build a fabric roll edge extractor
to replace the practice of labor operation in this procedure. The
fabric roll edge extractor will extract an adhesive tape from a roll
of fabric within 1 minute in an all-dry process. Full automation
processes can be replaced with the actual model in the current
human production line thus reducing operation cost and
human errors with higher efficiency.
OUR PROJECT SOLUTION
The device was divided into four mechanical processes
including tape locating, loosening, removing, and disposal,
respectively. After an array of research and analysis, we decided
to use a diffuse sensor for tape sensing, heat guns for tape
loosening, hook for tape removing, and pressurized air gun for
disposal.
FUTURE IMPROVEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
1. Vertical axis actuation of the extractor
2. Replacement of the sensor
3. Integrate the location of fabric edge with NFC module
4. Tape disposal with pressurized air nozzle
5. Setup a database for different fabric materials

What is Our Product?
Our product is a smart miniaturized Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) with a body design of the iconic Hong Kong trams. Our
mini AGV could move along a guided path and make its own decisions (turn left, right, or stop) autonomously. There is a open
compartment on the rear upper level of our AGV, which could be useful to better visualize actual-sized AGV. Furthermore, our
AGV has an Arduino-based controller, which could be easily programmed by the Block software.
Objective and Target Audience
Our objective is to create a STEM-oriented product that could increase students' interests in the world of robotics, logistics, and
automation. This product is targeted towards Primary and Secondary school educators who need a more fun and approachable
way. to introduce this technology to the newer generation. By combining the design of Hong Kong trams, the cultural icon of
Hong Kong itself, with this smart AGV, students would be more attracted and interested to learn more about AGVs and robotics
in general.

SMART MASK
Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, a face mask has help us to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 viruses. The use of the
mask has been substantially increased. For further enhancing the functionality of the mask, it is desirable for developing a
smart product with an integration of digital technologies, including loT, Al, mobile devices, and cloud computing. The
smart product has the following features to minimize the spread of the COVID-19:
• Monitor and record the air quality of the surrounding;
• Notify users if the surrounding air quality is not acceptable;
• Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating an easy identification of suspected users;
• Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
• Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
• Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.
SMART DESIGN
The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the
replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best
functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air
quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be
notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a
cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an
environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a
normal mask by removing the sensor part.

A competition-based platform for innovative young engineers
#HU HERKULES
Competition & Goals
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during
the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition
style, thus being exciting and unconventional.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and
restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to
gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A OHP enemy base is a
victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017.
We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical
experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into
technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm
development.
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of
development. It should also regulate the development so that it
proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical
and methodology knowledge.
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization
of development files
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details
that can be referred to during development to minimize
confusion.
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design.
These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance
solidarity.
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled
accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with
computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with
detailed plans before development. The plan is known as
software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key
technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carrier
out for fine-tuning.
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Mechanical & Hardware designs
The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each
of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
• Requirement list
• Mechanical layout & actuation plan
• Hardware schematic
The following are the examples of our design. They are:
• Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and
smart detection features
• Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for
defense
• Hero (bottom left): A heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
• Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special
projectiles to the Hero robot

Executive Committee: Muhammad Saad Shahid Anwel (President), Taha Abid, Le Chi Lim, Pawan Raskoti (Tech Leads)
Introduction
Key Technical Features
The world's fastest swimming robotic fish: a
robot that aims to mimic the propulsive
behavior of real biological fishes, designed to
swim in the complex dynamics of open
waters. Our fish swims at low frequency of 4
Hz, a cruising speed of 2m/s with an input
power of 150W, and can achieve high
acceleration with a compact and compliant
tail-like propulsor.
• Fully stable, buoyant, and waterproof
• All degrees of motion: roll, pitch, yaw
• Compact design with modular structure
• Energy efficient
Maneuverability at high speeds
• Arduino Uno & Raspberry Pi 4 with pi-
camera v2 module
• Wireless remote control
• Fins with servo control
Design & Manufacture
The latest version consists of about 250 individual
components assembled together. The dimensions are
1250mm x 150mm x 520mm with a mass of 13 kg.
The parts were 3D-modelled on SolidWorks, where
simulations were run to test the performance of the
fish body. A scaled-down version was 3D printed or
CNC machined for proof-of-concept.
The materials used to manufacture the robot are PLA
plus plastic, aluminium, rubber, and acrylic. Various
manufacturing methods have been used including 3D
printing, CNC machining, and traditional hand tooling
methods such as cutting, drilling, sanding, soldering,
etc. The electrical and electronic components such as
the motor, encoder, batteries, Arduino, Raspberry Pi
and the wirings are sealed in acrylic tubes.
Several versions of the robotic fish were built. Each
body differed in size and aerodynamic properties, with
tails varying in shape, size, and material to try to
achieve the best performance.
Fig 1. The robotic fish - latest design.
Remote Control
Implementation
• The controls are implemented through the
Raspberry Pi and Arduino, where the
Arduino is used mainly for GPIO to send
data to the Pi.
• A custom-built controller was designed
using the APC 220433M RF receiver &
transmitters (available with the Arduino).
• A custom communication mechanism
sends power signals and turning signals to
the fish. An auto timer is also implemented
to prevent the controller from overflowing
the buffer of the receiver.
• The orientation of the fish and fins is
controlled using input from motion and
orientation data, which is achieved with an
inertial measurement unit (IMU).
• The Pi utilizes its fast CPU to process the
data, controlling servos with input from the
camera while running machine learning
(ML) models.
• With the Sense HAT board, the Pi provides
an accelerometer and gyro which maintain
the orientation of the fish by a negative
feedback loop and servo (fins) control.
• Upcoming soon, we plan to perform
system integration to connect the control
systems and sensors of the robot with
computer vision components.
• We also aim to work towards deep
reinforcement learning (Deep RL) for
obstacle navigation.
Fig 3. Robotic fish tail.
Fig 4. Top view of the
newly added fins.
Factors Affecting Performance
The relation between body length and fish
swimming speed:
For a motor with given power and the same tail
design, an increase in length of the fish was found to
cause less vibration during motion. This is because
as length increased, the buoyancy, mass and inertia
increased as well. Hence, newer versions of the fish
were built with a longer body to improve speed.
The influence of tail design and amplitude on fish
swimming speed:
It was found that with a solid tail cannot make the
best of the motor. With the motor working against the
rigid tail, speed was reduced. To solve this, a flexible
3D-printed tail was built. The new tail can bend and
can absorb energy, significantly reducing the load on
the motor. The size of the tail was also increased, as
a bigger tail area allows it to push more water.
However, a size that is too large would increase the
load on the motor and ultimately burn it. Similarly, if
the amplitude of tail movement is too low, speed is
low, but if amplitude is too high, it increases load.
After testing several different tails and amplitudes, an
optimal design was finally achieved.

Background
Numerous blockchain systems with various consensus protocols
emerges to achieve high transaction rates (2~ 10K tps). However,
their underlying P2P network primitives constrain further
improvements due to high message redundancy and long
broadcast convergence time. The first problem is caused by the
excessive robustness of dominant broadcast approach Gossip. All
state-of-the-art blockchain systems only tolerate 20-50% node
failure while Gossip can withstand up to 90%. The reason for the
second problem is that existing broadcast topologies ignore
geographical distances among nodes and incur paths with
unnecessarily high latency.
Introduction to FRing
We present FRING, a geography-based P2P overlay network for
fast and robust broadcast in blockchain systems. FRING has three
main features: sufficient robustness, low message redundancy,
and fast convergence. To reduce convergence time, FRING forms
the network topology by considering geographical proximity. A
novel broadcast algorithm based on FRING topology is proposed to
lower message redundancy while maintaining sufficient
robustness. One major challenge is to eliminate the risk of
topology inference by traffic pattern analysis. FRING leverages Intel
SGX to guarantee nodes' behavior integrity and incorporates
pattern obfuscation to prevent the traffic pattern analysis.
Evaluation shows that FRING improved the throughput of EOS and
Hyperledger Fabric by up to 2.2X and 2.1X respectively.

Research Problems
Recent studies show that the underlying P2P network layer has
become the bottleneck for transaction rate. Current blockchain
systems form random P2P networks and predominantly use
Gossip as the broadcast mechanism for robustness. For each hop
in the broadcast process, a node pushes the message to a
randomly chosen subset of its neighbors or pull from the message
sender. There are two notorious problems associated with this
network solution.
1. Gossip generates excessive redundant messages because
Gossip is designed for extreme robustness (can tolerate up to
90% node failure). Such redundant messages lead to traffic
congestion under high transaction rates.
2. Random network topology causes unnecessarily long
broadcast convergence time (i.e. time used for a message to
cover all nodes in the network).
FRing: A Geograph-based P2P Overlay Network for Fast and Robust
Blockchain Systems
HUAWEI
Haoran Qiu, Tao Ji
Supervised by Dr. Heming Cui
Features of FRing
FRing addresses the two problems with three features:
1. Sufficient robustness: a broadcast operation can tolerate at
least the same portion of node failure as the blockchain
consensus protocol;
2. Low message redundancy: the messages generated in each
broadcast is efficient (O(N)); and
3.
Fast convergence: the convergence time are short enough so
that the accumulation of old messages is reduced effectively;
FRing Topology
Conceptually, the network topology of FRING is a selfmaintained
fractal ring structure, where lower level rings (typically formed by
inner-region nodes) reside on higher level rings (typically formed
by cross-region nodes) in a recursive way. To form this topology,
FRING groups all nodes based on their geographical proximity (per-
hop latency) at the bottom level. Each group forms a fully-
connected ring. FRING selects multiple nodes from each ring to
serve as representatives and they form a new ring in the higher
level recursively. Finally, there is only one global ring remaining at
the top level and all nodes are connected through representatives.

FRing Broadcast Mechanism
The broadcast mechanism of FRING is devided into three parts:
broadcast up, broadcast down, and broadcast within-ring.
Broadcast up and down are done with the help of representative
nodes. Multiple message paths increase the robustness, which is
also parametrized. Broadcast within-ring method is inspired by the
distributed k-ary search method which provides O(N) message
efficiency. It is done by constructing k-ary spanning trees.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques allow intra-operative monitoring of the ablation procedure during cardiovascular electrophysiology (EP). However, currently it is still

RoboFish
Presented by BREED HKU - bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong
Aim
This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore
the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
Our current objective through this endeavor is to
learn about the biomechanics of fish and other
underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand
how the movements are affected by different
variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The
model can be applied in surveillance systems and the
study of marine biology.
Hardware
RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered
by a battery.
The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that
moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion
of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was
designed by the mechanical team to translate the
rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion.
In the future, more features such as remote controlling
and surveillance systems aim to be added.
Figure 1. Initial Design.
Software
Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.
Background research on simulators.
Next stage:
Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment
of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the
model).
Through simulation, variation of different parameters of
the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed
and energy efficiency.
Design
The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess
the following characteristics:
Streamlined body.
Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between
separate components.
Low weight.
Floating stability and buoyancy.

ABSTRACT
Scoliosis is a medical
condition where a
person's spine has a
sideways curve. It
usually occurs before
puberty and prevents the
lungs from functioning
properly in severe cases.
Scoliosis is typically
diagnosed from X-ray
images, but diagnostic
X-rays increase the risk
of developmental
problems and cancer in
those exposed. This
project aims to obviate
children's X-ray
exposure in the early
diagnosis of scoliosis by
generating X-ray images
of children's backs from
the corresponding
harmless RGB-D images
rather than capturing the
X-ray images directly
from the children. An
RGB-D image of a back
combines a standard
RGB image with its
depth image, and the
depth image consists of
the distance between
each point on the back
and the camera to track
the spine. In this project,
a deep learning model
based on HRNet was
built and trained to
detect landmark
locations of the backs on
the RGB-D images first.
With the detected
landmarks, the X-ray
images of the children's
backs were eventually
synthesized from the
corresponding RGB-D
images by another deep
learning model that was
built and trained based
on the pix2pix model.
METHODS AND MATERIALS

images and anatomical landmarks
with Microsoft Azure Kinect DK
from Duchess of Kent Children's
Hospital and performed data
preprocessing.

and X-ray synthesis. The main
deliverables are two deep learning
models based on the HRNet and
the pix2pix model for landmark
detection and X-ray synthesis,

More on IMU
IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures
and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and
sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically
used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading
reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles
(UAVs), among many others, and spacecraft, including
satellites and landers. !!!
An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear
acceleration using one or more accelerometers and
rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also
include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a
heading reference. Typical configurations contain one
accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each
of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat
uses a library called RTIMULib to implement the interface
for reading from its IMU.

Func 1: Digital Level Meter
This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As
there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch
and roll values from the board. When the program detects that
roll is bigger than 45 or smaller than -45 degrees, the program
will switch to pitch measure mode. In this mode, a line will be
displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally.
When roll is between -45° and 45°, the program will switch to
pitch and roll measure mode. There will be two circles
displayed on SenseHat, and they will become closer if pitch
and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles
will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning
that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.

OUR PROJECT AIM
This project aims to design and build a fabric roll edge extractor
to replace the practice of labor operation in this procedure. The
fabric roll edge extractor will extract an adhesive tape from a roll
of fabric within 1 minute in an all-dry process. Full automation
processes can be replaced with the actual model in the current
human production line thus reducing operation cost and
human errors with higher efficiency.
OUR PROJECT SOLUTION
The device was divided into four mechanical processes
including tape locating, loosening, removing, and disposal,
respectively. After an array of research and analysis, we decided
to use a diffuse sensor for tape sensing, heat guns for tape
loosening, hook for tape removing, and pressurized air gun for
disposal.

4. Tape disposal with pressurized air nozzle

How does the fish turn?
The fish is turned left or right by controlling the tail movement through precise encoder
readings. The absolute encoder has 1024 steps to give very high accuracy. To turn, the speed
of the tail is adjusted in between a full cycle - tail going from one extreme to the other. When
the fish receives instruction from the controller to turn it moves relatively faster from one
extreme end (point A) to the other (point B). The arduino continuously updates the encoder
value at fixed intervals and when the encoder returns a value which signifies point B the power
is made lower depending on a value known as the turning differential. This turning differential
can be controlled by commands through the controller and determines the sharpness of the
turn.

What problems, did we have?
The rotary motion of the motor is converted to a linear motion allowing the fish to move left and right. Being
underwater, the force needed to propel the fish forward is large. The power provided from the Arduino
microcontroller to the motor will not be sufficient. Hence, we have used motor drivers to allow for higher powered
motors. The microcontroller will send PWM signals to the motor driver. A battery will be connected to the motor
driver and it will be the source of power for the motor. The driver will compare the signals from the microcontroller
such as off and on, and then regulate the power from the battery to the motor accordingly. The current fish uses a
motor driver that we have built from scratch. However, we intend to upgrade the driver to allow for higher powered
motors and for a more reliable system. We have tried using professional servo drivers such as the ESCON 70/10, but
it is too large to fit into the body of our fish. The electronics team is currently working on a more compact motor
driver.

Abstract
This project is a mobile application that aims to use AR visualization to teach the concept of
object and references using some mutable and immutable data types in Python as this is common
difficulty for beginner programmers. This app can execute supported Python code and present an
AR animation visualizing the underlying operations. The behavior difference between mutable and
immutable data types are shown using their AR models and animations. Sandbox mode and
exercise mode are available for user to explore on their own or follow exercises that showcase the
properties of the data types. The application is implemented on the iOS platform using RealityKit
and the Vision framework. While the application is adequate for learning the basic concept, the
support set of operation can be expand in the future for a more complete coverage.

Methodology
To illustrate the idea of objects and references, for each operation, a memory table will be
printed in AR to show what the operation is doing. The operation is animated as the Memory table
changes. For Lists, multiple List variables, as arrows, may point to the same location at the
memory table, where as non-mutable types such as Tuple will be shown as a taped cardboard box
that does not share its location with anyone.

Conclusion
As technology gets incorporated into the classroom, there is more research on what can be
used to enhance the learning experience.
Using AR in education is beneficial to students'
motivation to explore and help them come up with new hypotheses. It is suitable for learning
conceptual ideas.
This application aims to teach the relationship between the data and the operations for
mutable and immutable types in Python using AR. Through executing supported Python code,
the user is able to explore the properties of the variables. The visualization of these properties is
enhanced with the use or AR.
Objects of different types are given different AR models, and behave according to their
behavior in Python. The user is able to scan their own input or use input from exercise mode. User
can also read variable values with explorer mode in a more interactive way.
- Limitations: Limited Supported Operations
The application does not support all operations or data types in Python. Even for the supported
data types, not all built-in methods are supported. It would be beneficial to show which methods
are mutating.
- Limitations: Limited Interactivity
The scanning and execution of code are separated, and the user does not interact with the AR
scene physically once the animation begin. The core function of the application can be improved
in terms of interactivity, for example with markers that respond instantly.

World's Fastest Robotic Fish
CUINNESS
Team Supervisor: Dr. Zhang Fu, Department of Mechanical Engineering
Executive Committee: Muhammad Saad Shahid Anwel (President), Taha Abid, Le Chi Lim, Pawan Raskoti (Tech Leads)
Introduction
Key Technical Features
The world's fastest swimming robotic fish: a
robot that aims to mimic the propulsive
behavior of real biological fishes, designed to
swim in the complex dynamics of open
waters. Our fish swims at low frequency of 4
Hz, a cruising speed of 2m/s with an input
power of 150W, and can achieve high
acceleration with a compact and compliant
tail-like propulsor.
• Fully stable, buoyant, and waterproof
• All degrees of motion: roll, pitch, yaw
• Compact design with modular structure
• Energy efficient
Maneuverability at high speeds
• Arduino Uno & Raspberry Pi 4 with pi-
camera v2 module
• Wireless remote control
Fins with servo control
Design & Manufacture
The latest version consists of about 250 individual
components assembled together. The dimensions are
1250mm x 150mm x 520mm with a mass of 13 kg.
The parts were 3D-modelled on SolidWorks, where
simulations were run to test the performance of the
fish body. A scaled-down version was 3D printed or
CNC machined for proof-of-concept.
The materials used to manufacture the robot are PLA
plus plastic, aluminium, rubber, and acrylic. Various
manufacturing methods have been used including 3D
printing, CNC machining, and traditional hand tooling
methods such as cutting, drilling, sanding, soldering,
etc. The electrical and electronic components such as
the motor, encoder, batteries, Arduino, Raspberry Pi
and the wirings are sealed in acrylic tubes.
Several versions of the robotic fish were built. Each
body differed in size and aerodynamic properties, with
tails varying in shape, size, and material to try to
achieve the best performance.
Fig 1. The robotic fish - latest design.
Remote Control
Implementation
• The controls are implemented through the
Raspberry Pi and Arduino, where the
Arduino is used mainly for GPIO to send
data to the Pi.
• A custom-built controller was designed
using the APC 220 433MHz RF receiver &
transmitters (available with the Arduino).
• A custom communication mechanism
sends power signals and turning signals to
the fish. An auto timer is also implemented
to prevent the controller from overflowing
the buffer of the receiver.
• The orientation of the fish and fins is
controlled using input from motion and
orientation data, which is achieved with an
inertial measurement unit (IMU).
• The Pi utilizes its fast CPU to process the
data, controlling servos with input from the
camera while running machine learning
(ML) models.
• With the Sense HAT board, the Pi provides
an accelerometer and gyro which maintain
the orientation of the fish by a negative
feedback loop and servo (fins) control.
• Upcoming soon, we plan to perform
system integration to connect the control
systems and sensors of the robot with
computer vision components.
• We also aim to work towards deep
reinforcement learning (Deep RL) for
obstacle navigation.
Fig 3. Robotic fish tail.
Fig 4. Top view of the
newly added fins.
Factors Affecting Performance
The relation between body length and fish
swimming speed:
For a motor with given power and the same tail
design, an increase in length of the fish was found to
cause less vibration during motion. This is because
as length increased, the buoyancy, mass and inertia
increased as well. Hence, newer versions of the fish
were built with a longer body to improve speed.
The influence of tail design and amplitude on fish
swimming speed:
It was found that with a solid tail cannot make the
best of the motor. With the motor working against the
rigid tail, speed was reduced. To solve this, a flexible
3D-printed tail was built. The new tail can bend and
can absorb energy, significantly reducing the load on
the motor. The size of the tail was also increased, as
a bigger tail area allows it to push more water.
However, a size that is too large would increase the
load on the motor and ultimately burn it. Similarly, if
the amplitude of tail movement is too low, speed is
low, but if amplitude is too high, it increases load.
After testing several different tails and amplitudes, an
optimal design was finally achieved.
Fig 5. INU for motion control.
Achievements
THE VAYU PROJECT
1. Guinness World Record holder for "The fastest 50m swim by a robotic fish".
2. "Caudal-Fin based Turning Mechanism for an Underactuated Fast Swimming Robotic
Fish" published at the International Conference for Marine Robotics 2019 held on
September 17-19, 2019, at St. Petersburg State Marine Technical University, Russia.
3.
"Development of High Performance Mechanical Robotic Fish" published in the 8th
PAAMES meeting and AMEC held on October 9-12, 2018, in Busan, South Korea.
Fig 2. A successful body and tail design.
Use Cases
Surveillance and Data Gathering
• Unregulated fishing practices have
reduced fishery resources in local waters.
As a surveillance device intended for data
collection and marine research, our fish
can be used to monitor illegal fishing.
• Top-notch surveillance using computer
vision technology can be used to look for
illegal fishers and detect entangled fish in
broken fishing nets.
Plastic Collection
• We aim to use this technology to tackle
marine litter and water pollution, a serious
issue with huge environmental impact.
• Computer vision can be geared towards
the detection of plastics, with a garbage
collector added to the fish to gather litter.
Oil Spills
• Oil spills may take weeks or years to clean
up. Using a swarm of "oil sharks", this
could be possible in just a few days,
minimizing severe environmental effects.
• The technologies of UV fluorescence
analyzer or non-dispersive/fixed filter IR
analyzer can be adapted to the fish for oil
detection in water.
Aquaculture
To improve fishing and aquaculture
processes, the robotic fish can use its
speed and vision technology to survey the
bottom of trawling nets
• The fish can also serve as an ultrasonic
bot to assist in the clean-up of biofouling
(harmful buildup on fish nets).

and interactive future of clinical practices, with specific focus on head-and-neck surgeries.

Padmanabhan Kishoth/Lui Wing Ming/Tam Ho Kai/Tam Chun Fai/ Ng Hon Fai
Supervisor: Dr M.M.Y. Choy
Department of Mechanical Engineering
INTRODUCTION
• Cake decoration is an art which can take many
years to perfect, even for a professional pastry chef.
• 3D printer technology is a novel creative solution to
help bakers master cake decorating skill.
• Advantages over the traditional approach include
speed and accuracy, so that complex design can be
more easily achieved.
• This study aims to modify an existing 3D printer to
make it compatible to extrude food material to
decorate the top and side walls of a Cake.
METHODS
• A Rheometer is used to measure the fluid
properties and analyse compound chocolate and
Nutella for decorating.
RESULTS
• Results reveal that paste extruder can successfully print simple to
complicated designs using both Nutella and chocolate icing on the top
surface of the cake.
• Hot-melt extruder can print 3D compound chocolate using dark and
milk chocolate models to decorate both the top and side wall of cake.
• An extruder is a component on 3D printer that
ejects out materials. Modified extruders are used in
form of Syringe paste extruder which prints 2D
edible food paste.
• Combining both one can achieve in decorating the top and sidewall of
the cake which could be potential in usage in baking quicker, tasty
and more complicated designs for amateur bakers and pastry chefs
• Hot melt extruder to print 3D edible chocolate
models.

Triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is a new promising energy harvesting
technology that can produce electrical energy. A TENG makes use of the

electrical energy. This project aims to design and fabricate a wearable
TENG that can be mounted on the human body as the electrical power
source of electronics. With the aid of energy harvesting technology, a
self-powered load-suspended backpack is developed and it can detect
shoulder misalignment. Meanwhile, the load suspended system allows the
reduction of vertical oscillation during the walking motion.

Basic TENG configuration
deformation of brush
A TENG consists of two dielectric materials and they are connected to a
circuit. When two bodies are brought into contact, triboelectric charges are
induced on the surfaces. After separating the two materials, a potential
difference is induced between the two electrodes. To maintain electrostatic
equilibrium, the electron tends to flow to the other side through the external
circuit and current is induced. In our design, Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)
and nylon brush are adopted. Compared with the traditional design, the
brush-type structure allows deformation such that the surface contact area
increases and facilitates the power generation of TENG. A multi-layered
pattern is also adopted in the design to improve performance. The TENG
can generate 1.912 W in 20 minutes.

Shoulder misalignment detection design
Working principle of the detection system
Unlike the convention detection systems, the design involved no microprocessor
and sensors. A white Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe is bent into 10-degree to form
a V-shaped structure. Clamped. Both interiors of the caps and the pipe are at-
tached with copper tape for electrical conduction. A steel ball is also placed
inside. When the user exhibits shoulder misalignment, the backpack is tilted such
that the steel ball is rolled to the side due to gravity. The steel ball acted as a switch
and completed the circuit of the system by touching the cap and pipe at the same
time. As a result, the electrical energy generated by the TENG is discharged and
actuates the LED to warn the user. With such a design, the system only consumes
0.32 W and fulfills the power supply of TENG.

Introduction & Story
FOOD City PANDA Run! is a 3D Runner Game developed during the course of COMP3329 Computer
Game Design and Programming. The game idea is actually drawn from a book-keeping app called
Fortune City which applies gamification of personal finance managing. We aim to apply a similar
design to food delivery apps such as foodpanda, that the game can be embedded to those apps to
meet business objectives as retain current customers and attract new ones.
The background story goes as follows. In 20 AC (After Covid), Hong Kong is under a great
depression of economy and food supply. To make ends meet, the player has to take a part-time job as
a food delivery guy. However, in today's world, even the slightest mistake can lead people being fired,
to make sure all the food reaches their customers intact, the player must avoid all obstacles
appearing on their road of delivery...
Technical Specifications and Assets Used
FOOD City PANDA Run! is developed on Unity game engine and used c# as scripting language. All
assets were purchased on unity asset store, including Hong Kong Street (for overall game scenes),
Japanese School Lunch (for food choices), and Mobile Traffic System (for player car). For sound effect
of the game, such as background music and coin collect effects, we referred to some online open
source of audio materials. Some sample game scenes and assets are shown below:

Game Logic
1. The player initially has 3 food on the tray for delivery.
2. The player can move Left or Right by pressing - and →, or A and D, to avoid hitting the obstacles
and to collect coins as delivery tips.
3. If the player have a minor or indirect collision (like pushing) with the obstacle, it will push the
obstacle away without punishment.
4. The food will drop from the tray if the player hit directly with the obstacle. The number of food
that drops depends on how hard the player hit the obstacle.
5. The player fails the game if there is no food left on the tray.

Team Member: Hu Zhenwei
Supervisor: Prof. Reynold Cheng
In Hong Kong, the number of elderly citizens is estimated to rise to 1/3 of the population (2.37 million) in
year 2037. As they age and become more frail, the damand for support services (e.g. providing domestic or
escort services) will increase significantly in the coming years. However, there is a severe lack of manpower
to meet these needs. Some elderly-care homes reported a 70% shortage of employees. There is thus a strong
need of voluntary or part-time helpers for taking care of elders.
HINCare is now downloadable in Apple and Google Play Store, it has been serving more than 2000 elders and
helpers in NGOs (e.g., SKH and CFC). The app is designed with large fonts and spacing for the ease of elder users.
The system attracted media attention, and won the Asia Smart App Award 2020 - Merit Award and the Faculty
Knowledge exchange Awards 2021 HKU. HiNcare is extended to support community investment and inclusion runa
(CIIF), a government funding agency and its associated NGOs in 2021.
We introduce HINCare, an app that encourages mutual-help in the community. HINCare adopts the
concept of timebanking, where each user has his/her own account to store the amount of time ("time credits").
Users earn time crealts by providing services to others. The user can use the time credits to purchase other
services. Moreover, HINCare uses HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) to recommend helpers to elders.

meet customized needs of the elders and find the best helpers to assist the elders. Our team use HINs and Al
technologies for matching elders and helpers. It is based on our recent research results.

antibiotics and other antimicrobial compounds. Harmful microbes acquire resistance genes
that grant them immunity when exposed to antimicrobials. This has led to the concerning
emergence of drug resistant bacteria or "superbugs". The WHO declared AMR to be in the
"top 10 global public health threats facing humanity"
However, the risk from this menacing phenomenon is not restricted to human health. It is a
threat to the environment and environment-dependent industries such as the food industry,
which predicts massive production, economic losses, and food safety concerns.
The effects of AMR can be observed on a local scale as well within the Pearl River Delta. In
Hong Kong, resistance surveillance in food done between December 2019 and June 2020
revealed that out of the 851 raw beef, chicken, and pork samples tested, 80.1% tested
positive for resistant strains. Similarly, out of the 304 samples of vegetable salad, salmon
sashimi, and tuna sashimi tested, 15.1% were positive for resistant strains.

Project Description
AMPed - Our Solution
Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs)
Addressing the challenge of superbugs and meeting the demand for alternatives are a class of
compounds called Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs). AMPs are innate defense proteins that
have broad-spectrum antimicrobial with high targeting specificity, due to their ability to
distinguish pathogenic cell membranes from host cell membranes. Most importantly AMPs
are significantly more difficult to develop resistance towards. Our AMP of interest Cecropin
B hails from the Cecropia moth and has proven to be highly and broadly effective against
microbial pathogens
Microalgae
To complement our powerful AMP, our chassis of choice eventually led to Chlorella vulgaris
var. autotrophica. Its low susceptibility to AMPs and efficient expression of complex proteins
made it an ideal chassis for the expression of Cecropin B. Compounding Chlorella's known
high growth rate, low maintenance cost and straightforward culturing as well as a high
nutritional value to the consuming species, it has potential for application as a fish feed
supplement in aquaculture, agriculture and even human consumption.
Two-Pronged Application
AMPed integrates Cecropin B and Chlorella into two potent applications: The Secretion
Model uses Chlorella as a protein factory, producing Cecropin B in high quantities to be
purified for a multitude of downstream uses. The Encapsulation Model takes advantage of
the nutrition and robustness of Chlorella to carry Cecropin B internally as a capsule which
can convey passive immunity through a supplement or feed product.
Expansion plans
While project can be expanded upon with little effort and minimal financial strain, there is still
work to be done. The completed product needs extensive laboratory testing to ensure maximal
nutritional value and antimicrobial effect. The production pipeline needs to be streamlined to
ensure fast and efficient manufacturing. Field trials also need to be conducted to witness the
Chlorella in action in a real world setting so that inputs can be obtained from end users to make
final adjustments to suit the needs of the consumers. The project must be also scaled up to
industrial levels to meet demands from the markets.

job. A wooden bottom plate is also included for
consolidating the whole placement design and

inside Mai Po Natural Reserve is the main

open intertidal mudflat without vegetation since
waterbirds need to feed and roost on this
intertidal mudflats.

deploying labour in vegetation removal in the
intertidal mudflat, increase the efficiency in
vegetation removal and raise the safety of the
worker.

Competition & Goals
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during
the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition
style, thus being exciting and unconventional.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and
restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to
gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A OHP enemy base is a
victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017.
We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical
experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into
technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm
development.
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of
development. It should also regulate the development so that it
proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical
and methodology knowledge.
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization
of development files
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details
that can be referred to during development to minimize
confusion.
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design.
These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance
solidarity:
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled
accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with
computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with
detailed plans before development. The plan is known as
software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key
technical aspects within cach step and node. Testing is carrier
out for fine-tuning.
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Mechanical & Hardware designs
The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each
of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
• Requirement list
• Mechanical layout & actuation plan
• Hardware schematic
The following are the examples of our design. They are:
• Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and
smart detection features
• Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for
defense
• Hero (bottom left): A heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
• Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special
projectiles to the Hero robot

Student name: Tam Yung Yip, Supervisor: Dr. C.K. Lee
Abstract
SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) technology, which
combines mapping with robot localization[1], can help solve the
problem of developing accurate environmental maps for robots in
unfamiliar environment. This project aim to construct a robot using
SLAM and a monocular camera for depth estimation. The system will
be able to map the environment correctly and robustly, determining the
robot's location and orientation inside it. Then, the robot is capable to
estimate the depth using a deep learning model and pictures recorded by
the monocular camera as input for further 3D environment construction.
PID control on the car base control
The PID method, which stands for proportional, integral, and derivative,
will be utilized to minimize mistakes in motor speed control.
Proportional gain shortens the control system's reaction time, but if it is
set too high, the system may become unstable. Integral gain can be
aggregated with each speed increase to reduce steady-state inaccuracy.
Derivative gain is used to reduce system stress and can dampen the
system. The PID algorithm combines these three parameters to provide
fast, accurate, and consistent outcomes.

U-Net structure of monocular depth
estimation
The U-Net model is commonly utilized in computer vision tasks for
depth estimation. It obtains the contour of the picture by extracting
features from two same-size upsampling and downsampling layers,
which is then processed through the network's encoder and decoder
sections with the ReLU activation function[2]. The U-Net model
takes a single RB picture as input and returns a depth map that
represents the distance between items in the scene and the camera. It
extracts features using convolutional layers and reconstructs the
depth map using deconvolutional layers while maintaining spatial
information and incorporates global context.

project, we now continue on our B-MAT system.

# FINISHED SUBPROJECT: AMPed
The project tackled the aquatic aspect of the local environment. The emphasis was on the
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) which is a phenomenon in which harmful microbes acquire
genes resistant to antimicrobials. The effect of AMR has been observed in the local Pearl
River Delt a region. The fish industry is meanwhile heavily influenced by AMR as microscopic
pests that infect fish can not be countered by conventional means.

The solution provided is the transgenic AMP-expressing microalgae fish feed supplement
that delivers passive immunit y and nutrition to fish in aqua systems plagued with AMR. In
the project, our team focused on the expression and production of Cecropin B (CecB) in the
microalgal chassis Chlorella vulgaris var. autrophica (Chlorella). CecB is an ant imicrobial
peptide(AMP) found in the Cecropia Moth (Echelon Biosciences, 2022), with innate broad-
spectrum antimicrobial activities and rare inferrals of resistance. We introduced it to the
pisciculture industry as a fish feed supplement by designing two forms of products- the
AMP isolate powder and the microalgal protein with the AMP encapsulated.

Battery recycling in Hong Kong has gained increasing attention during rapid
industrial development. Currently, the two mainstream methods to recycle
rechargeable batteries - hydrometallurgy and pyromet allurgy both come with
negative environmental impacts. As an alternative, bioleaching is a recycling
method that uses microbes to recover useful metals in batteries in a cost-
effective and eco-friendly way. But current practice of bioleaching exhibits
two main problems: (1) Slow reaction kinetics, (2) Bacteria have low tolerance
towards oxidative stress, hindering the scalability of the technology.

ONCE THE WORLD'S FASTEST ROBOTIC FISH --
NOW READY TO DOMINATE THE SEA.
Objectives
• Enhance manoeuvrability to navigate through real-world terrains
• Improve waterproofing technique for continuous deployment in water bodies
• Increase robustness and efficiency of mechanical/electrical system
• Increase controllability by providing better user experience
200000m
7000
BREED HKU
Swimming across the harbour from Central to TST, our robotic fish will prove
its applicability in seawater.
Along with its previous speed record and additional features, it can be
beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere
with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is
also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
• The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.
• We have developed full motion control of the robotic fish with the aid of Motor
Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY
controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to
provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable
configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for
communication.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
• Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water
current is reduced.
• With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with
3D printing only.
• The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to
overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
• The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion
with a very low energy loss.
• From the previous testing, our chassis is certified to be completely waterproofed
for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time
of at least 2 months.

The Problem
• Tenants' rights are disorganised and
confusing.
• Tenants avoid suing their landlords in fear
of being kicked out, which means that their
rights in law are not enforced.
• Disconnection between tenants and those
responsible for protecting their rights since
it is difficult to report and detect breaches
Our Solution
• Database of regulations on health and
safety.
• Computer vision: our platform recognises
objects and links them to the
relevant health and safety provisions.
• Reporting breaches: our platform has the
contact details of those in charge of
rectifying each specific breach in order to
better connect tenants with the authorities.
Tenants can also create an anonymous
report to avoid being punished by landlors.

WOO Chung Yu, NG Ka Lok, YIP Tsz Fung, CHEN Wu Juang, CHING King Him, L Jason Chun Lok
INTRODUCTION
Research works in deep reinforcement learning have been emerging, however, only
few of them actually demonstrate results on real physical agents. Duckietown Project
provides an opportunity to properly benchmark the current state of the art of these
methods as applied to real robotics system. The mission of our project is to
democratise Artificial Intelligence (Al) and robotics research. Through this project,
students gain tangible experience in a fun way in assembling self-driving robots and
applying Al to the physical education platform developed by MIT.

Supervisor:Dr. Jia Pan, Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science
Student Representatives: Tingxiang Fan, Sirui Chen, Jialong Li, Chuek Yin Chui
Introduction
ICRA Al Challenge is a worldwide college
students robotics challenge held by IEEE
Robotics and Automation society and DJI.
Each
team represents a university which need to
program two purely automatic robots and
compete with other teams in a RTS game
manner. Deep learning and other Al related
technology will be used. The challenge will be
divide into three sub-topics: Decision making:
Perception and Navigation.
RVO Diagram
Decision Making
We uses behavior tree for decision making.
compared with FSM and decision tree, this
approach can support realtime decision
making as well as making the code portable
Navigation
To make our robot more agile in planning
as well as deal with narrow space and
dynamic obstables we implemented a
parallel heuristics based rapid exploring
randon tree (RRT*) algorithm in
cooperate with Local Reciprocal Velocity
Obstacle multiagent collision free policy.
Diagram for Behavior Tree
Perception
We design an efficient object detection
and tracking algorithm combining kernalized
correlation filter tracker and SVM+ HOG
detector as well as parallel programming
logic. The tracking pipeline can be run at
140 FPS, which significantly boost up the
system response.
Dinarin of Navigation Pipeline:
Diagram of Parale RRe
Perception Pipeline
Conclusion
We ranked 10th over 80+ international teams
and won the excellent prize in robot navigation
algorithm design competition. All the members
envolved has got hand on experience of doing
large scale programming project and learnt how to
work in a team with git.
For technical part, since this year's competition
has been moved online, the practical testing
regarding some algorithms robustness is still
undetermined, which will be implemented and
tested next year. Moreover, the decision making
pipeline currently is not scalble to more complex
tasks, which remains to be optimized next year.

MEW provides an intuitive visual interface for

Methodology
Development
The software was developed in 2 stages:
Stage l: Minimum viable product version of the
software built with HTML, CSS and JS. Less framework
for rapid iteration. Limited Scratch integration.
Stage 2: A more polished version built with React.
Integrated directly into Scratch by creating a fork of
the Scratch GUl repo and rebuilding all the features
from stage 1. Many important new features that
were requested in stage 1 testing were also added.
Conclusion
Findings
MEW's visual interface helps beginners feel more at ease
when interacting with this new technology. The open-
ended nature of the software allows users to experiment
with Al by making projects that are personally relevant.

HEARTFUL: DEVELOPING A COUNSELLING
LLM VIA API AND PROMPT ENGINEERING
Kim lan, Wang Liheng Grace, Dr Kevin Wu, Dr Lei Yang
Introduction
Large language models (LLMs) play a central role in
our daily lives, and its integration has revolutionized
Motesses
This has been used in many applications such as
customer support, education, with some even using
it for chatbots for mental health.
However, a shortcoming in the use of such models
for counselling purposes is that, while it is able to
simulate empathy through language, the responses
are safe but generic that ignore specific nuances or
factors (i.e. an inability to read between the lines). It
is thereby unable to provide true "genuineness"
specific to a client.
We therefore introduce our model Heartful to
overcome such limitations, where it is created to
provide remedial counselling services with
psychotherapeutic concepts in mind.
Future directions include the offering of tools such as
grounding exercises, cognitive reframing prompts,
and behavior planning, while maintaining a
supportive, non-judgmental tone. We thus discuss
the impact of Al on counselling techniques.

insulation coating
• Less loading on cables
Integrated Drone:
• Drone includes wheels and coating mechanism
• Yaw to attach/detach, the coating mechanism is
housed in a clamp
• Simpler mechanism and operation

River Restoration and HE
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large
upper section of concrete streambed (Fig 2(a)). However, this design
hinders HE
which results in bad river eco-system. HE transports
suspended and dissolved solutes such as nutrients, contaminants,
organic carbon, and oxygen into the HZ. HZ creates a rich biocenosis
composed of species that temporarily and permanently dwell there. In
recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the
recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still
missing.
Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of
different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and
groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with
floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

In this project, our team aimed to enable a quadruped robot to navigate various
terrains without relying on visual input. To achieve this, we studied a paper called
"DreamWaQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain
Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning" and utilized Beta Variational
Autoencoder with a policy network to help robots interpret their surrounding
environment using past proprioceptive data.
How it works:
the Encoder receives 5 proprioceptive past observations that can be obtained
inside rovot's internal sensor. The , the encoder produces a vector "z" that
represents robot's imagination of the environmen. Finally, based on the vector z,
the policy produces 12 angle joint values for the robot to move.

CAPSTONE PROJECT
GROUP DO4
PROJECT TOPIC
Development of Universal Testing Machine with
Digital Image Correlation System for Soft/Biomaterials
Performing tensile testing using a Universal Testing Machine or lensile testing machine related to the
measurement of displacement and strain is the basis for defining the mechanical properties of a biomale-
rials, which allows scientists and researchers to understand how they can utilize the material and engineer
it for different purpose, also the first step of developing a new biomaterial.
DEPARTMENT OF MECHANICAL ENGINEERING
The University of Hong Kong
OUR OBJECTIVES
The capstone project team will develop a universal testing machine specifically for soft and biomaterials
with the minimal scale and production cost, such that in order to increase the availability of the universal
testing machine, and enhancing the development and the rescarch on the new biomaterials.
In addition to the development of UTM, the team will also investigate and provide an overview on the possi-
bility of integrating the contactless optical measurement technique.
TESTING PROCEDURES
How to use the Universal Testing Machine to perform
tensile testing together with Digital Image Correlation Analysis
1. Sample preparation (Applying black speckle patterns on testing sample by using airbrush)
2. Fixing the sample on the grip
3. Applying load to the sample and Capturing the images during elongation
4. Processing images
5. DIC Analysis and Post-DIC Analysis
6. Computation of Stress-Strain Curve

mechanically intensive. We have designed an additional beat-mapper program to translate music pieces into

Introduction
Video games have always been a popular proving ground for artificial intelligence tech-
niques. Traditional Al agents have relied on scripted, rule-based approaches that have sev-
eral flaws. Recent breakthroughs have come through the application of novel machine
learning approaches. In our project, we implement neuro-evolution using NEAT and rein-
forcement learning using Sarsa(lambda) to the real-time strategy game, StarCraft II, which
is claimed to be the next "grand challenge" for artificial intelligence. Specifically, we apply
it to micromanagement in StarCraft II which involves the small-scale precise control of in-
Neuro-Evolution
Methodology
The neuroevolution approach combines neural networks with evolutionary algorithms.
Through the NEAT algorithm, neural networks are dynamically generated and optimized
across the training process. The NEAT algorithm in particular evolves both the weights as
well as topology of the networks based on the fitness (performance) of the networks on the
given tasks
NEAT-SC2 Framework
Open-Sourced framework developed to expedite the NEAT training and evaluation pro-
cess for StarCraft II
Features
Launch configurable StarCraft Il games through PySC2
Launch NEAT trainings fully configurable through the
command line
Visualise training process
Checkpointing to pause and resume trainings
Evaluate trained agents in independent or
Caree
ensemble control

Focus on good Software Engineering
principles: Extensibility, Agent Decoupling
NEAT Agem
NEAT Agent
Neural Network Inputs - Current Health, Weapon Cooldown, Weapon ranges (Self/Enemy),
Movement Speed (Self/Enemy), Enemy in-range, Recurrent Previous Command, Distances
to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs
Neural Network Outputs - Fight/Flee, Displacement in x-axis, Displacement in y-axis
Results
The NEAT Agent successfully learnt the kiting/hit-and-run strategy for a ranged vs melee
matchup in a restricted space. It learnt the optimal kiting strategy for different kind of
ranged units which was robust to different starting configurations. The evolved microcon-
troller performed well even if the number of enemy units was increased. In addition, net-
works were also evolved to learn the melee-vs-ranged matchup
Deliverables
Applied Neuroevolution and Reinforcement Learning to SC2 micromanagement
Built frameworks for machine learning agents to interact with SC2
Generic training agents with helper functions to speed up development
Trained agents that successfully learnt strategies for micro-scenarios
StarCraft Il Map sets

Reinforcement Learning
Methodology
Reinforcement Learning aims to find a policy for an agent to maximise its reward
in its environment. We applied the Sarsalambda) algorithm to micromanage-
ment in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that
uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit
Sarsa Agent

Scaled Relative Power, Is Together, Weapon Cooldown

Results
The Sarsa Agent was applied to various complex scenarios that required creative
micromanagement strategies such as kiting/hit-and-run, effective unit position-
ing, attack timing and evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of yourself
versus the enemy. The agent successfully learnt optimal strategies for all scenari-
os tested

Our implementations show the potential of neuroevolution and reinforcement learn-
ing for complex control problems. Through effective experimentation in StarCraft II,
one can transfer the findings of this project to real-world problems such as evolving

ABSTRACT
A procedure for the seismic analysis of underground tunnels using recorded free-field earthquakes based
on the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach is presented. The near and far fields of the half space are
lisplacement on the near-field boundary are computed for each spectral frequency of the carthquake
Then, equivalent seismic forces are computed for the near-field boundary for the earthquake spectrum.
By assuming the soil-tunnel system to be uniform along the tunnel axis, the 2.5D approach can account
for the wave transmission along the tunnel axis, which reduces to the 2D case for infinite transmission
velocity. The horizontal and vertical components of the 1999 Chi-Chi Earthquake (TCU068) are adopted
as the free-field motions in the numerical analysis. The maximal stresses and distribution patterns of the
tunnel section under the P- and SV-waves are thoroughly studied by the 2.5D and 2D approaches, which
should prove useful to the design of underground tunnels.

BookNotes
Introduction:
Taking notes for books in an organized manner has always been a hard work. Not only will the
notes be lost, but they are also hard to search with. Sometimes you can't even write on a
borrowed book. BookNotes utilizes rectangular detection to allow users to scan a page of the
book and take notes on the image easily. Users can also type additional notes and add tags to
facilitate searching. Users can organise the notes according to the book they belong to by simply
scanning the barcode of the book, then the details of the books are filled in automatically.

Introduction:

sample series of short audio recordings that are looped back continuously. This allows users to
gradually build layers of sounds and music on their own until all the recordings combined sound
comparable to a complete band or musical piece
Currently, such technology in its physical form is very expensive (~4000HKD), hence
inaccessible to most. In light of this, Loopit aims to make such technology accessible to the
casual user.

various health problems including depression, obesity and having metabolic syndrome. There are

together to form lunch date groups. The app features instant multiple matching. Whenever you
would have lunch, launch the app, then we will make all the arrangements for you.

Our music game sets out to improve everyones burst typing speed and stability.
Developed with Node.js, Expressjs and SocketO, Lost Slime is a Multiplayer/Educational/Rhythm game that runs on
your web browser. Written in javascript, it is designed to be lightweight and responsive to run on any machines.
Find Slimies new houses! Players in a game room compete to stack the tallest pillar to gain a high ground - which
helps Slimies in spotting new locations to house. To stack a pillar block, players time their space-bars along with the
music beats. But that's not it! There are phrases or sentences intertwined with, that players have to input correctly
before pressing space-bar! By achieving the two objectives, Slimies can then jump on the newly stacked pillar block!
With the theme set as improving everyone's typing proficiency with music, it could be cheerfu-lighthearted, or
mechanically intensive. We have designed an additional beat-mapper program to translate music pieces into
custom track information used by the game, in json format. Which means players can create authentic mappings
with their favorite music! We sincerely you could enjoy the game and offer us your precious like!

Development of Universal Testing Machine with

Performing tensile testing using a Universal Testing Machine or lensile testing machine related to the
measurement of displacement and strain is the basis for defining the mechanical properties of a biomale-
rials, which allows scientists and researchers to understand how they can utilize the material and engineer
it for different purpose, also the first step of developing a new biomaterial.

The University of Hong Kong
OUR OBJECTIVES
The capstone project team will develop a universal testing machine specifically for soft and biomaterials
with the minimal scale and production cost, such that in order to increase the availability of the universal
testing machine, and enhancing the development and the rescarch on the new biomaterials.
In addition to the development of UTM, the team will also investigate and provide an overview on the possi-
bility of integrating the contactless optical measurement technique.

Introduction
Video games have always been a popular proving ground for artificial intelligence tech-
niques. Traditional Al agents have relied on scripted, rule-based approaches that have sev-
eral flaws. Recent breakthroughs have come through the application of novel machine
learning approaches. In our project, we implement neuro-evolution using NEAT and rein-
forcement learning using Sarsa(lambda) to the real-time strategy game, StarCraft II, which
is claimed to be the next "grand challenge" for artificial intelligence. Specifically, we apply
it to micromanagement in StarCraft II which involves the small-scale precise control of in-
Neuro-Evolution
Methodology
The neuroevolution approach combines neural networks with evolutionary algorithms.
Through the NEAT algorithm, neural networks are dynamically generated and optimized
across the training process. The NEAT algorithm in particular evolves both the weights as
well as topology of the networks based on the fitness (performance) of the networks on the
given tasks
NEAT-SC2 Framework
Open-Sourced framework developed to expedite the NEAT training and evaluation pro-
cess for StarCraft II

NEAT Agent
Neural Network Inputs - Current Health, Weapon Cooldown, Weapon ranges (Self/Enemy),
Movement Speed (Self/Enemy), Enemy in-range, Recurrent Previous Command, Distances
to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs
Neural Network Outputs - Fight/Flee, Displacement in x-axis, Displacement in y-axis
Results
The NEAT Agent successfully learnt the kiting/hit-and-run strategy for a ranged vs melee
matchup in a restricted space. It learnt the optimal kiting strategy for different kind of
ranged units which was robust to different starting configurations. The evolved microcon-
troller performed well even if the number of enemy units was increased. In addition, net-
works were also evolved to learn the melee-vs-ranged matchup

in its environment. We applied the Sarsalambda) algorithm to micromanage-

uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit

Our implementations show the potential of neuroevolution and reinforcement learn-
ing for complex control problems. Through effective experimentation in StarCraft II,
one can transfer the findings of this project to real-world problems such as evolving

River Restoration and HE
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large
upper section of concrete streambed (Fig 2(a)). However, this design
hinders HE
which results in bad river eco-system. HE transports
suspended and dissolved solutes such as nutrients, contaminants,
organic carbon, and oxygen into the HZ. HZ creates a rich biocenosis
composed of species that temporarily and permanently dwell there. In
recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the
recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still
missing.
Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of
different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and
groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with
floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

The ACSS aims to reduce man power needed in preparation work of conference seats. It is started in 2019 by

fully automatic system for preparation work for events in conference room. There asre two main functions to the
system: Stacking up chairs and de-stack columns of chair.
STRUCTURE OVERVIEW
The structure is separated into three moveable parts,
designing for the simplest amount of motions needed for
transporting the chair. The electrical part is also kept as
simple as possible for smoother and safer operation.

ROBOTIC ARM STRUCTURE
The transportation of chair heavily depends on robotic
arm, so we need a robotic arm with high durability and
strength to overcome the deflection and weight of chair
during operation.
Primary Actuator
Secondary Actuator
Each robotic arm is made with 1 L-shape aluminum plate,
2 rails and 3 aluminum bars. The middle bar with the L-
plate attached is able to be moved forth and back while
the other two are fixed.
To move the clamps horizontally, two 200mm travel
length ball screw actuators are used. The actuators are
programmed to move in opposite directions, in order to
contract and release the clamps. Each actuator is able to
carry loads up to 30kg.
SEPARATING MECHANISM
The separators aim at overcoming the pressure between
chairs to separate them from a column. The separators
are made using 3D printer and installed in the middle of
the clamp. They are motor driven and rotatable and
rotate between the gap of two chairs to overcome the
frictional force between the chairs.
To move the clamps in forward direction, rack and
pinions are used. The meshes of the gear and rack give

Touchscreen has become a standardised

mobile device by touchscreen instead of allowing them
to interact with virtual objects in reality.

MULTIPLAYER MODE
Our Multiplayer mode links the positions of different play-
