THE EDUCATIONAL POSSIBILITIES OF
AR
AR simulations enable students to observe phenomena
they would not be able to see first-hand. E.g. laboratory
experiments may be too costly.
SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
1. HAND GESTURE RECOGNITION CONTROL
Gesture-based control methods provide players a more natural and
realistic approach to interact with virtual game objects. In addition,
players can have 3d control with their hands over the real space in-
stead of 2D control over touchscreens. This project will not create a
new hand tracking and recognition system, but aims to integrate ex-
isting hand gesture recognition control systems as the main input
method in a bid to create an immersive gaming experience.
2. WORLD MAP SHARING AMONG DEVICES
The key to make an immersive AR game is to integrate multiplayer
functionality in AR gaming development. Multiplayer mode re-
quires a network to link the position of each player, sharing the
same world map across different mobile devices. The APls in
ARCore and ARKit have similar functions but they are plat-
form-specific. To better advance the existing APls, this project
aims to build a multiplayer functionality that can achieve a shared
world map. In conclusion, this project focuses on three major as-
pects, which include a cross-platform AR developing framework, a
HGR control scheme, as well as a cross-platform shared world map
for multiplayers.
ABSTRACT
With the increasing popularity and computation
power of mobile devices, AR (Augmented reality) is
more accessible. It has a high potential for revolute
human-machine interaction. Video games, especially
mobile games, can utilize AR technology to provide
an immersive user experience. Without using expen-
sive high-end AR devices such as HoloLen, mobile AR
experience usually lacks interactions between users
and virtual objects due to limited size and control
interface of the device. This project is to develop an
AR interactive mobile game prototype under a
cross-platform development framework and in-
cludes hand gesture control and world map sharing.
We developed an Android AR game application pro-
totype using ARFoundation in Unity. A hand gesture
control scheme is built using the Manomotion SDK.
The world map sharing is achieved using Google
Cloud Anchor API and the multiplayer functionality
was done by using Photon Bolt.

Our project seeks to alleviate some of the health threats in Southeast Asia
due to limited acces to roads and healthcare facilities. It suggests the use
of drones to deliver medical supplies. The design of our drone service differs
from existing companies because it proposes larger service areas,
incorporates the idea of a telemedicine service to reduce the need to travel
for medical consultation, focuses on a supplier-to-patient network structure
rather than a supplier-to-hospital network structure, and suggests using public
health centers and small clinics as delivery centers if patients do not have access
to phone or internet.

> Technology <
Our current prototype involves a latching mechanism that uses a servo motor to
grab the box in place, securely and safely. Our prototype will be able to catc
h and release the load from our base station to a set point with or without supervision.
With more funding, we will investigate and experiment new forms of loading mechanisms
as well as other drone technologies to ensure a more reliable and smooth delivery.
With the rise of 5G and Al, we can form a network of drones to deliver medicine to

> Plan of Action <
Once our drones and latching mechanism have been designed and successfully test
ed, we are hoping to implement this project in parts of Southeast Asia that are
particularly disadvantaged in terms of access to roads and medical services.
Specifically, we have identified the regions of Ratanak Kiri in Cambodia, and West
Kalimantan and Riau in Indonesia as potential implementation areas. In this later
phase of the project, we will seek to work with local governments to obtain the necessary
permissions to operate our drones (e.g. commercial licenses for drone use) and help
deliver medical products to public health facilities. We will be relying on different sources
of funding for this later phases of the project. In particular, we will be applying to the
Gallant Ho Experiential Learning Fund, as well as funding from the Tam Wing Innovation Wing.

Globally, depression is a prevalent neurological disorder and can cause severe

cost on the undiagnosed patients are substantial[2). Currently, the prevention and
diagnosis technologies lack a way to raise self-awareness and provide trigger-

ordinary people a way to make trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary

During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of disinfectants has surged in order to contain the
spread of the virus. Many disinfectants will be sent to wastewater treatment plants after use for
treatment before discharging back to the environment. Nevertheless, studies have shown that
large amount of disinfectants can inhibit biological reactions during the wastewater treatment
process. The activated sludge process is particularly susceptible to disinfectants. Hence, this
study aims to investigate the inhibitory effects of two common active ingredients of
disinfectants, namely QACs and sodium hypochlorite, on the activated sludge process.

Under the Hong Kong law, students should not harass or vilify any other
students. If a student does so and the act leads to physical harm, the student
could potentially face legal consequences. It's important to note that a school is
generally not liable for acts committed by its students. However, if a school has
knowledge of discriminatory acts committed by its students and fails to take any
action, the school may be liable for discrimination (Source: Their son has been
teased by his classmates because of his disability. Is the school liable for acts of
harassment and vilification committed by a student against another student with
a disability?').
If legal action is initiated, it may lead to a court hearing where all the
circumstances of the incident will be examined. If you are under 25, and the
court decides to sentence you, it could result in an order for detention in a
reformatory school, a detention centre, training centre, rehabilitation centre or
place of detention (Source: 'Orders for Detention'").
It is crucial that you report this incident to your school and parents, if you haven't
done so already. If the school is informed, they can take steps to manage the
situation, potentially avoiding escalation to legal proceedings. If the school fails
to take action after being informed, they may be held liable under the DDO
(Source: "Their son has been teased by his classmates because of his disability. Is
the school liable for acts of harassment and vilification committed by a student
against another student with a disability?').

Ian Lo Leong Ting, Nafis Ul Islam, Yoko Lau Tsz Ching
Background
Robotic arms have been widely used in various real-world
scenarios, such as automobile manufacturing and
housekeeping. However, there is a significant gap at the
Innovation Wing, as existing robotics-focused projects mainly
focus on mobile robots or quadrupeds. To address this gap,
our project aims to develop an intelligent manipulator
capable of performing precise tasks like maintenance and part
sorting in industrial settings.
"A digital twin is a virtual representation of an object or system
designed to reflect a physical object accurately. It is updated
from real-time data and uses simulation, machine learning and
reasoning to help make decisions." - IBM
Digital Twin Entity
Potentials
• Enables operators to remotely monitor the real arm's
performance in real-time, ensuring human presence is
minimized in potentially dangerous areas.
• Provides a safe environment for planning and testing
operations before execution.
• Facilitates efficient decision-making through simulation,
machine learning, and reasoning.
Visualization Results
• Our ROS package includes visualization capabilities using
RViz, enabling users to observe the robotic arm's
movement and behaviour in real-time.
• We continuously update the step-by-step teaching
materials, empowering users to effectively learn and
understand complex robotic arm controls through hands-
on experiments.
Key Features
• Versatile Control:
Our package offers various control methods, including:
• Joystick control for precise end-effector coordinate
manipulation
• Sliding bar control for accurate joint angle adjustment
• Click & Go interaction for seamless positioning.
• Leader-Follower Capability: allows either the physical or
the simulated arm to take the lead, while the other arm
acts as a follower. This flexibility enables collaborative
tasks, where the digital arm can guide the physical arm's
movements or vice versa.

stability across various terrains. By mimicking natural
animal gaits, IK improves the robot's ability to navigate
obstacles and interact effectively with its environment.

navigates stairs using articulated legs for enhanced
stability and flexibility. Equipped with advanced motion
control algorithms, it could potentially handle complex
terrains, making it ideal for search and rescue, industrial
maintenance, and surveillance in inaccessible areas.

SUSTAINABLE WEEDING SOLUTION
INNOGROW
Abstract
Sustainable farming is gaining traction in Asia to address weed challenges that hinder crop growth. Traditional weed
control methods often rely on toxic chemicals that are unsustainable in the long term, negatively impacting soll health
and reducing fertility. Therefore, there is an urgent need for innovative weed elimination methods that do not depend on
these conventional solutions.
We propose a compact, versatile weed-killing device that easily attaches to various farming equipment, such as harrows,
tractors, or ATVs. Utilizing an affordable camera and advanced computer vision, the device accurately detects weeds,
which are then targeted by a laser based on gathered positional data. Housed in a lightweight unit powered by a
compact processing unit, it ensures speed and efficiency
Our innovative device offers a cost-effective solution for small farmers, enabling effective weed management without
chemicals. This approach enhances crop yields, improves the quality of life for both farmers and consumers, and
promotes environmental sustainability, supporting the transition to more sustainable farming practices.
Weeds are a major threat to crop production
• Competition for Resources
• Reduced Crop Quality
• Reduction in Crop Vields of 20-60% in key crops
• Increased Production Costs
• Harboring Pests and Diseases
• Annual global economic losses exceeding $30 billions
Traditional weed control methods
Chemical
• Toxic exposure to farmers
• Residues in food/water
• Herbicide resistance

Why ventilation matters?
Although airborne transmission of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has already been acknowledged by leading health authorities, no existing standard
for building ventilation yet considers the need to control respiratory infection. The speaker shall explain why outdoor has a lower infection risk than indoor, and why poor ventilation can
worsen both short- and long-range inhalation. The speaker shall present a new equal CO2 exposure method to derive a set of minimum ventilation rates and associated maximum CO2
concentrations in indoor settings with various activity levels (rest, light-, moderate- and heavy-exercise) and breathing modes (breathing, speaking, singing and loudly speaking).
Opportunities for innovation will be mentioned.

Image Recognition, Classification

BUILD SMART - INNOVATION IN CONSTRUCTION
2:00-3:00pm • April 28, 2021 (Wednesday) • Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing or via ZOOM
Construction and infrastructure make significant contributions
to
economic growth and social development. In Hong Kong, the annual
construction output will reach HK$300billion in the coming years.
However, the construction industry in many economies face significant
challenges such as labour shortages, an ageing workforce and cost
escalation, which hamper the enhancement of productivity and
sustainability. Various innovative approaches have been developed,
spearheaded by modular integrated construction (MiC), coupled with
the adoption of many smart technologies such as Al, loT, VR, robot,
Digital Twin, etc. This workshop aims to systematically explore the
knowledge, theory, and technology solutions of innovation in
construction and infrastructure development. The workshop will first
define the key concepts within their theoretical contexts. We will then
examine the smart technologies adopted in construction with
demonstration cases. Innovations and technologies will be illustrated
using various real-life projects. Metaphorically, MiC acts as an aircraft
carrier to drive smart technologies which act as fighter aircrafts, in
return, to safeguard and empower MiC in transforming the industry
towards sustained success. The workshop will also explore the
prospective development of innovation by sharing the latest research
and development led by CICID and MiC Lab of HKU.
Speaker:
Professor Wei Pan
Professor and Executive Director
Centre for Innovation in Construction and Infrastructure
Development, Department of Civil Engineering, HKU
Moderator:
Professor Thomas Ng
Associate Dean of Engineering (Student Development) &
Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, HKU

The Rainbow Passage
When the sunlight strikes raindrops in the air, they act as a prism and form a rainbow.
The rainbow is a division of white light into many beautiful colors. These take the
shape of a long round arch, with its path high above, and its two ends apparently
beyond the horizon. There is, according to legend, a boiling pot of gold at one end
People look, but no one ever finds it. When a man looks for something beyond his
reach, his friends say he is looking for the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
Throughout the centuries people have explained the rainbow in various ways. Some
have accepted it as a miracle without physical explanation. To the Hebrews it was a
token that there would be no more universal floods. The Greeks used to imagine that
it was a sign from the gods to foretell war or heavy rain. The Norsemen considered
the rainbow as a bridge over which the gods passed from earth to their home in the
sky. Others have tried to explain the phenomenon physically. Aristotle thought that
the rainbow was caused by reflection of the sun's rays by the rain. Since then
physicists have found that it is not reflection, but refraction by the raindrops which
causes the rainbows. Many complicated ideas about the rainbow have been formed
The difference in the rainbow depends considerably upon the size of the drops, and
the width of the colored band increases as the size of the drops increases. The actual
primary rainbow observed is said to be the effect of super-imposition of a number of
bows. If the red of the second bow falls upon the green of the first, the result is to give
a bow with an abnormally wide yellow band, since red and green light when mixed
form yellow. This is a very common type of bow, one showing mainly red and
yellow, with little or no green or blue.

From hospital-centric to human-centric:
Personalized wearables for digital healthcare
The soaring population aging, the quarantine and the shortage of medical instrumentations are demanding decentralized medical technologies that can enable remote and personalized healthcare. Wearable
technologies are the protagonists. Emerging wearable devices include, but are not limited to, smartwatches, smart clothing, smart glasses, smart jewelry, and wearable cameras. Some of these wearables can
already measure vital signals such as heart rates, breathing rates and blood pressure. Moving forward, next-generation wearables are expected to enable on-demand blood tests and continuous recording of our
electrophysiological signals for disease screening and monitoring. However, several challenges remain.
in this workshop, the speaker will describe how wearable technologies are impacting our healthcare systems, how to develop a wearable device, how we can address the most pressing challenges with
transdisciplinary biomedical engineering approaches, and finally. how Biomedical Engineering can ultimately improve the human health.
